root_cause_chain: Twenty-five runs isolated the failure layer by layer: network fine (socket trace ok), httpx fine (identical-client trace 403), host loop fine (request trace showed claim/get/report working). The real defect was worker containers lacking config.yaml — deps.get_config() raised 503 inside NativeWorkerHost.execute(), the refusal loop left the run pending, and the visible ConnectError spam was only the controller's own 300s timeout teardown. Fix: materialize config.yaml from the archived config.example.yaml in every two-host native container before pytest (commit 30f55042f).
other_fixes_this_slice: redis pinned image id; migration container stdin staging; scheduled-package import cycle (tasks-before-runs via importlib, isort-proof); RunContext/DbRunEventStore/ThreadMetaRepository import paths; UUID owner with resolvable email; workspace scope around create_or_reject; port-open gate before starting the worker; host/worker addresses parameterized via env
boundaries: Deterministic C graph only — no real model, no AIO sandbox execution yet, no scheduler occurrence, no B integration in this slice (B side proven by slice 1). Remaining two-host work: C1(AIO tool)→B→C2 scheduled occurrence chaining, real Scheduler launch, cross-host revocation/restart recovery, then M5-M11. Tenant activation false.
debug_instrumentation: The worker test retains the traced request wrapper, socket/httpx watchers and the swapped identical client from the diagnosis; they document the isolation chain and are inert when the loop is healthy.
